Singapore reached its target of 10 total trees this pass (7 already published + 3 shipped: sgp_008 Bodhi Tree of Pearl's Hill, sgp_009 Banyan of Tiong Bahru Park, sgp_010 Earpod Tree of Fort Canning). The remaining ~147 unique register candidates (of 163 within 5km, after removing 13 rows that matched already-published trees by coordinate) were not individually verified this pass, per the brief's 'no more than 10 total' instruction. Listed below are the strongest-looking clusters for a future deepening pass, not individually fetched/verified.

leads.note: 2026-08-30 deepen pass (verify): shipped 4 trees to data/research/singapore-verified.json, sgp_019-sgp_022 (African Butter Tree/Healing Garden, Teak/Botany Centre, Nemesu and Mengkulang/Rainforest edge), all extending the same Botanic Gardens cluster inward from the Lawn O / rainforest-edge candidates this file already flagged. All four use heritagetrees.nparks.gov.sg as one source plus a genuinely separate independent source (PROSEA for the African Butter Tree, Wikipedia's Tectona grandis for the Teak, sbg.nparks.gov.sg's own visitor list for the Nemesu, and a 2022 NUS/Kew peer-reviewed paper on Singapore type localities for the Mengkulang, which is the strongest single source found this pass: the Mengkulang is the actual type specimen from which Heritiera elata was described to science in 1908). Stopped at 4 per this pass's time-box, not because candidates ran out.

leads.cluster: Kempas, considered and set aside this pass
candidates: HT 2016-280 Kempas (Koompassia malaccensis), near the Fernery / Lawn O, Singapore Botanic Gardens (1.310508, 103.817405)
leads.reason: Fetched and read (heritagetrees.nparks.gov.sg profile: girth 3m @1.3m, height 36.6m, endangered emergent species, buttresses to 6m). Register location_text says 'Lawn O' while the NParks profile page itself says 'near the Fernery' for the same ht_id, a minor internal inconsistency worth a glance on the ground. Set aside this pass only because no genuinely independent second source (beyond the NParks profile and a generic Wikipedia species page for Koompassia malaccensis) turned up in the time available, not because of any evidence problem; a future pass should try iNaturalist observations or a Singapore nature blog before shipping it.

blocked.name: Ordeal Tree (Erythrophleum suaveolens)
blocked.location: Singapore Botanic Gardens, National Orchid Garden Nursery
blocked.reason: NParks own citation page states plainly: this Heritage Tree is not accessible to the public (it stands in the working nursery area of the National Orchid Garden, not the visitor garden). Blocked under hard rule 10 (access), not an evidence problem: girth 5.6m, height 28m, more than 100 years old, transplanted from the former Economic Garden before 1920 ahead of the Raffles College development -- all well documented if the access situation ever changes.
